title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board met Tuesday night and picked up where they left off in April with friction between some board members and the village attorney.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order with one member, Trustee Beth Prosser attending remotely.  She joined fellow Trustees Sue Lindeman, Jim Duff and Larry Phillips.  Travis Strausbaugh and R.C. Franklin were absent.

The first order of business was the approval of the agenda and past meeting minutes and the bills.  Mayor Delonshaw then called on James Murphy with Leymone Hardcastle & Company CPA’s to present the annual village audit.  Murphy went through numerous pages of financial information for the period ending April 30, 2026, and pronounced the audit as clean with only minor findings and thanked the office personnel for their help and assistance.

Mayor Delonshaw asked the board to consider a request by the owner of 300 Circle Drive to allow for a camper dump.  The matter was brought to light at the April meeting but further clarification was needed before any action was taken.  With the questions answered the mayor asked trustees whether to allow the proposal to go forward.  He stated that if approved, they would need to install a check valve to prevent sewage backflow at their own cost.  He further opined that any new sewer customers should also be required to install a check valve to prevent future problems.  It was also said that a monthly fee needs to be charged to allow the uncommon practice and it needs to be regulated only for personal, occasional use.  When a motion was made with the stipulations cited and applying a $5 monthly fee, the measure passed unanimously.

Next, Village Attorney Barry Bright was prepared to offer an ordinance concerning the disposition of past closed session minutes and the verbatim audio tapes that are required to memorialize those sessions.  Bright cited the need to take action at previous meetings and discussions became somewhat heated over what is contained in the recordings, no action was ever taken while the attorney formulated an ordinance to deal with the situation.  Bright had invited trustees to listen to the recordings, but that apparently hasn’t happened.  Trustee Sue Lindeman was unwilling to authorize the destruction of the tapes without knowing what they contained and made a motion that the minutes and the recordings should all be made public.  Attorney Bright then presented a document that he said was prepared with AI (Artificial Intelligence) that examined whether the verbatim recordings can be released publicly and whether any municipality in Illinois has ever released the contents of the audio tapes that are maintained for a period of 18 months.  He stated that his legal advice is that they cannot release the content of the recordings and urged them not to do so.  Lindeman persisted and Trustee Jim Duff seconded her motion and the measure passed unanimously.  Bright then turned to Mayor Delonshaw and Clerk Shannon Hall and told them not to allow the tapes to be accessed by the board.  Lindeman then objected and stated that Bright had told them that they could listen to them.  He said he was rescinding that permission and if members persisted, they would need to seek a court order to allow them access to the recordings.

Next, the issue of selling the property at 400 S. Main St to the high bidder was again a topic of discussion and possible action.  In April, Fellowship Church, (formerly Clay City Methodist Church) was the lone bidder with an offer of $7,500.  When questions arose about the purchase and demolition costs the village has incurred and whether the village could reacquire the property should the church close, no action was taken.  Church leaders were to discuss the proposed stipulations with their congregation and then report back if the details were acceptable.  Attorney Bright and Mayor Delonshaw say the bill of sale is not yet finalized but the church has agreed to the changes including the right of first refusal.  A brief flare up occurred when legal fees were mentioned in relation to the total costs associated with the purchase of the property and demolition costs.   In the end, the board voted to authorize the mayor to formalize the verbal agreement.

Village Clerk Shannon Hall briefly went over the monthly cash balances and transfers report and then requested to attend the Illinois Rural Water Association Administrative Conference July 16 and 17 in Effingham and trustees approved her request without dissent.  On the topic of water, a question came up concerning the amount of water loss reported in April, which was some forty percent higher than the previous month, or some 861,000 gallons of water, which the village paid for to EJ Water.  Utilities Superintendent Sean Sullens noted that there were two issues responsible for most of the loss.  First was a four inch waterline at Bradford Supply and a residential issue elsewhere in the village and repairs have been made.

Before adjourning, Trustee Larry Phillips brought up nuisance properties, or specifically nuisance vehicles that are not running, have no license plate and no wheels.  After a short discussion, the village will send out letters to the property owners and if no action is taken, the issue will be turned over to the sheriff for removal at the owner’s cost.  Phillips also mentioned nuisance properties at the corner of 7th and Main and on 4th street with letters to be sent to the owners demanding compliance with village ordinances.

title: RIVERA PLEADS GUILTY
full_story:
44-year-old Arnold Rivera, Jr. of Vandalia was sentenced to a total of 75 years in prison for murder and criminal sexual assault.

Rivera plead guilty Tuesday in Fayette County Circuit Court to the murder of 14-year-old Kylie Toberman of Vandalia in November.

Judge Allan Lolie sentenced Rivera to 60 years in prison for the murder and to 15 years in prison for the criminal sexual assault.  Rivera will serve the murder sentence in its entirety and will serve 85% of the criminal sexual assault.  Also, the sentences will be served consecutively which Judge Lolie explained would have Rivera in jail for around 72 years.

title: OVERSTREET TO ADMINISTER OATH
full_story:
Justice David K. Overstreet of the Illinois Supreme Court will administer the attorney’s oath to 12 new lawyers this afternoon, in the Fifth Judicial District.

The group is among 279 individuals who will be sworn in and admitted to the practice of law in Illinois during bar admission ceremonies held in the state’s five Supreme Court judicial districts.

The bar admission ceremony in the Fifth Judicial District will begin at 2 pm at the Cedarhurst Center for the Arts located at 2600 Richview Road in Mt. Vernon.

Justice Overstreet will preside over the ceremony.  Laura Beasley, Chair of the Fifth District Character and Fitness Committee, Sarah Taylor of the Illinois State Bar Association Board of Governors and J. Nelson Wood, Chairperson of the Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission, will serve as speakers.

William Richardson, the former Deputy Chief Counsel for the Department of Corrections, will make the motion to admit the class.  The motion will be seconded by Jerome McDonald, an attorney at Black, Ballard, McDonald, P.C.

Guests of the Illinois Supreme Court will include Fifth District Appellate Court Justice James Hackett, Fifth Judicial Circuit Chief Judge Mark Bovard, Twentieth Judicial Circuit Associate Judge Alana Mejias, Fourth Judicial Circuit Judge Bradley Paisley and Second Judicial Circuit Judge Jo Beth Weber.

Justice Overstreet will rule on the motion, administer the attorney’s oath, and make remarks.  A reception hosted by the Illinois State Bar Association will follow the ceremony.

All of the candidates have passed the Illinois State Bar Examination and a required ethics examination and were certified by the Supreme Court Committee on Character and Fitness.

The Fifth Judicial District is composed of 48 counties including, Clay, Effingham, Fayette, Jasper, Jefferson, Marion, Richland, and Wayne.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
USDA’s latest crop progress and condition report released Monday showed 24% of corn and 26% soybeans had emerged in Illinois, both well ahead of the five-year average of 9% and 7%, respectively.

Planting progress reached 38% complete for corn, close to the 36% average, and 46% complete for soybeans, compared to the average 32%.

There were 2.7 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending May 3rd.  Statewide, the average temperature was 54.5 degrees, 3.4 degrees below normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.84 inches, 0.69 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 3% very short, 10% short, 70% adequate, and 17% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 17% short, 65% adequate, and 13% surplus.

Corn planted reached 38%, compared to the 5-year average of 36%.  Corn emerged reached 24%, compared to the 5-year average of 9%.

Soybeans planted reached 46%, compared to the 5-year average of 32%.  Soybeans emerged reached 26%, compared to the 5-year average of 7%.

Winter wheat headed reached 56%, compared to the 5-year average of 28%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 2% very poor, 5% poor, 18% fair, 67% good, and 8% excellent.

title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and moved swiftly through their agenda and are making way for many activities in the coming weeks.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and recognized visitors.  Chris Schoo with Louisville American Legion Post #914 presented a plaque to Mayor Spicer in honor of the City of Flora’s support of the “Be the One Walk,” the effort to call attention to the problem of Veteran suicide in America.  Schoo thanked them and encouraged everyone to join them and Flora American Legion Post #14 and participate in the third march from Flora to Louisville this Saturday, March 9 at 8:00am starting at the World War II Memorial at Flora’s Library Park and ending at the Veterans Memorial at the Clay County Courthouse in Louisville.  Lunch is served at the Louisville American Legion following the event and participants will be taken back to Flora afterwards.  It is reported that 6,000 Veterans take their own each year in the United States.  Mayor Spicer thanked Schoo for the award and implores everyone to join them and wishes them success in their effort.

Next, Kristen Logan with the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders addressed commissioners seeking their approval of the use of the Clay County Fairgrounds for their annual Crain-Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo.  The event is planned for Friday, July 24 at 7:00pm to kick off the 2026 Clay County Fair and features not only Bull Riding, but also Barrel Racing, Mutton Busting, the popular Rodeo Clown and the Bit Drill Team.  Logan noted the pre-sale tickets are $12 and $15 at the gate.  Kids 5 and under are admitted free.  She also assured the council that everything is pretty much the same as in previous years and their insurance is up to date.  They are encouraged by the increasing popularity of the event and their attendance numbers have been good.  She also stated that the Clay County 4H Barbecue will take place the same day from 4:00-7:00pm at the REA Building.  Commissioners quickly approved Logan’s request.

Flora’s Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart filled in for former commissioner Mike Genthe to represent the Clay County Cruisers Car Club.  Rinehart explained the club is requesting to use Charley Brown Park for their 22nd Annual Car and Truck Show on Saturday, July 25 from 9:00am-2:00pm.  Rinehart earned unanimous approval for the event.

Mayor Spicer then asked and received approval of the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included past meeting and hearing minutes and the April warrant list.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer thanked the Flora Rotary Club for installing the new bathrooms at the Pickleball Courts which she adds are now open.  The mayor also thanked the Flora Coon Hunters Club for their events hosted at Charley Brown Park.  She added that City Administrator Mike Stanford paid a visit to the hunters during their recent event and the club presented him with a plaque, thanking the City of Flora for its support.  Mayor Spicer noted the coon hunters love coming to Flora and they bring many visitors to our community, and in turn, they spend not only their time in Flora, but also their dollars.  She also encouraged residents to get ready for Spring Clean Up coming May 18.  Details are available on the city website, florail.govoffice2.com.  It also includes B & H Recycling returning to town on Saturday May 16 from 9:00-11:00am at the old Clay Medical building just off E. North Ave. in downtown Flora.

Next, Mayor Spicer asked and commissioners approved naming Maralee Johnson, Robbin Dickey and Joe McCoy to the Flora Public Library Board of Trustees for a three-year term that ends April 30, 2029.  They also approved naming Jane Blanchette to the Flora Public Library Board of Trustees to complete the term of Karen Briscoe, which ends April 30, 2027.  Council members also ratified the resignation of Debbie Lamb from the Flora Tourism Committee, effective April 19.

In polling commissioners for their comments, Jeremy Henderson took a moment to congratulate all graduates for their accomplishment.  Other commissioners echoed Henderson’s sentiments.  Commissioner Phil Wiley commented on the number of activities quickly approaching, including Springfest on Saturday, May 16 at Flora’s Library Park.  The Barbecue Cook Off will feature many participants as well as other vendors and merchants offering spring products for sale such as patio furniture.  There are also lawn games and inflatables for the kids.  Don’t forget about the 10th Annual 6K Walk for Water at 9:00am at First Christian Church of Flora.  Wiley also presented a resolution to adopt the revised Net Metering Policy for 2026, and the measure was approved without dissent.  Commissioner Lacey Lewis added to Wiley’s list of upcoming activities.  She said that Flora Tourism is hosting a fundraiser at St. Stephen’s Church to help pay for this year’s Flora fireworks display.  Salt and Strings Butchery is offering a curbside pork steak dinner with potato salad, baked beans, roll and dessert for $15.  Drive-thru serving runs from 4:00-7:00pm.  Tickets are available from Lacey Lewis, Phil Wiley, Ted Whitehead or any Tourism Committee member, the Flora Chamber of Commerce or at Salt and Strings.

Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford again noted the recycling event is coming up Saturday, May 16 from 9:00-11:00am and will accept a laundry list of items.  Details are available on the city website.  He also noted that B & H Recycling now charges for the items they accept.

Stanford also presented an ordinance approving the awarding of the bid and sale of the property at 121 W. Maple St. to Anthony Booth for $2,000.  Commissioners approved the measure unanimously.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles stated that the Flora Swimming Pool is on schedule to open on Saturday, May 23.
